Each area of `src/scgsim` owns one part of the work from a layout to a report,
and a change keeps that part where it is. This page says, for each area, what
it must not take over and which area owns that instead. What each folder does,
and the order the work flows through them, is in the
[code map](code-map.qmd#stage-tables); this page does not repeat it.

## What each area must not take over {#scgsim-2.0-ownership}

| Area | Must not take over | Owned instead by |
|---|---|---|
| `scgsim.geometry` (`source`, `interpretation`, `junctions`, `surface_epr`) | Building the 3D model; Palace or AEDT physics; execution state | `geometry/sgb`; the backends |
| `scgsim.geometry.models`, `geometry.exact`, `geometry.grid` | A second definition of a record the stages share | Nothing else: each record has one definition here |
| `scgsim.geometry.sgb` | Meshing; solver state; the layout and component source | `meshing`; the backends; the PDK and the `GeometryPlan` |
| `scgsim.meshing` | Palace attributes; solver state; a judgment of physical convergence | `palace/mesh`; the convergence declaration of a run |
| `scgsim.semantics` | Mutable backend objects; a solver tag read as source truth | The backends, which keep tags as observations |
| `scgsim.contracts` | Any other code of `scgsim`, and the numeric, layout, plotting, meshing and solver libraries | Nothing: the files between stages are defined here alone |
| `scgsim.palace.simulation` | Submitting a solve; one merged state for both problems | Whoever runs the handoff `palace/run` writes |
| `palace/source`, `palace/mesh`, `palace/config` | Each other's step: the geometry request, the mesh, `config.json` | The stage named for that step |
| `palace/run` | Submitting the solver; reading results | The person who runs it; `palace/results` |
| `palace/results`, `palace/reports` | Running the solver; a physical quantity common to every solver | Palace itself; each backend's own reports |
| `scgsim.aedt.specs`, `aedt.preparation` | Desktop or runtime state; the state of `EigenmodeSim`; solve results | `aedt/runtime`; `aedt/eigenmode.py`; `aedt/results` |
| `scgsim.aedt.runtime` | Building geometry; physics that crosses solver families | `geometry/sgb` builds the model AEDT imports |
| `aedt/batch.py`, `aedt/batch_stages.py` | Building the model or a Desktop; scheduler submission; one project for several models | `aedt/runtime`; the caller |
| `scgsim.aedt.epr` | Building, solving and exporting a plain Eigenmode design; the Desktop's lifetime; result custody | The HFSS family of `aedt/runtime`; `aedt/results` |
| `aedt/results`, `aedt/presentation` | Running a solver (results); native calculations and validation (presentation) | `aedt/runtime`; `aedt/results` |
| `scgsim.visualization` | Solver state, run status or physical acceptance | The backends and their results |
| `scgsim.presentation` | Domain projections or scientific calculations | Each backend's reports |

The import contracts of the [order CI checks](code-map.qmd#checked-order)
enforce the rows that are about imports; the other rows are kept by review.

## State boundaries {#state-boundaries}

- Palace Electrostatic, Eigenmode and Driven keep separate mutable state and
  fall back separately when a setting changes, on one shared core
  (`palace/simulation`, [lifecycle](architecture.qmd#palace-preparation-lifecycle)).
- Gmsh runs in fresh worker processes: the meshing round
  (`meshing/driver.py`) and Palace's group lowering (`palace/mesh/process.py`).
- AEDT `EigenmodeSim` keeps mutable configuration; one transaction
  (`aedt/runtime/transaction.py`) owns every receipt change and the Desktop's
  lifetime ([AEDT lifecycle](architecture.qmd#aedt-execution-lifecycle)).
- A geometry snapshot is detached from the objects it was made from, and a
  backend tag is an observation, never the source of an identity.

A change that moves code keeps these boundaries and the failure order they
define.

## Outside SCGSim {#outside-scgsim}

[OrcaPen SC PDK](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/orcapen-sc-pdk) owns the
component geometry, the material and stack facts, and the public
component-simulation notebooks; SCGSim keeps no copy of a notebook
([notebook contract](notebook-contract.qmd)). Native Palace and AEDT are
installed by their user; SCGSim never installs them and never runs a handoff
on its own. A Python script
or notebook calls SCGSim directly, with no parent workspace.
